title: Recognition over a local ring and its henselization
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A,k)$ be a commutative local ring with residue field $k$ [def-weil-residue-field], let $H$ be its henselization [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] with residue field identified with $k$, and let $K/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $C$ be a henselian local commutative $H$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] such that $H\to C$ is local and ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Suppose $q:C\to K$ is surjective, $\ker q=\mathfrak m_C$, and $q$ composed with $H\to C$ equals $H\to k\hookrightarrow K$. Regard $C$ as an $A$-algebra by composition. Then $A\to C$ is local and ind-etale. For $R=A,H$, let $D_R$ be the ring colimit of etale residue triples over $(R,\mathfrak m_R,K)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-residue-triples], with its induced residue map $q_R:D_R\to K$. There is exactly one $R$-algebra isomorphism $a_R:C\xrightarrow{\sim}D_R$ with $q_Ra_R=q$. In particular $C$, with the specified residue map $q$, is a strict henselization of both $A$ and $H$ in the pointed-algebra colimit sense [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The map $a_A$ respects the canonical $H$-structure on $D_A$ induced by the universal property of the henselization: $a_A\circ(H\to C)$ is that canonical local map $H\to D_A$.

proof.text: Write $\eta:A\to H$ and $h:H\to C$ for the structure maps. Apply [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] at $\mathfrak m_A$. Here $A_{\mathfrak m_A}=A$ canonically: every denominator outside $\mathfrak m_A$ is already a unit, so $a/s\mapsto as^{-1}$ is the inverse localization map. Thus $\eta$ is ind-etale. Composition stability in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] and the assumed ind-etaleness of $h$ show that $h\eta$ is ind-etale. It is local since $(h\eta)^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\eta^{-1}(\mathfrak m_H)=\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), property (2); Tag 0BSI (lemma-composition-colimit-etale); Tag 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h), final sentences

proof.text: For each $R\in\{A,H\}$, the specified embedding of its residue field $k$ into $K$ is a separable closure. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] to $(R,\mathfrak m_R,K)$. It gives a filtered etale presentation of $D_R$, a surjection $q_R:D_R\to K$ with kernel its maximal ideal, a local structure map $R\to D_R$, and henselianness of $D_R$. The composite $R\to D_R\to K$ is the prescribed $R\to k\hookrightarrow K$: it is induced by the evaluations of the triples, all of which have that composite.

Fix $R=A$ or $H$. Both $C$ and $D_R$ are henselian local ind-etale $R$-algebras. Use the identifications $C/\mathfrak m_C\xrightarrow{q}K$ and $D_R/\mathfrak m_{D_R}\xrightarrow{q_R}K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with source $C$, target $D_R$, source prime $\mathfrak m_C$, and residue map the identity of $K$. The primes contract to $\mathfrak m_R$, and residue compatibility follows from the prescribed maps $R\to k\hookrightarrow K$. It gives a unique local $R$-map $a_R:C\to D_R$ with $q_Ra_R=q$. Apply the same node with source $D_R$ and target $C$ to get $b_R$ with $qb_R=q_R$. The maps $b_Ra_R$ and $\mathrm{id}_C$ both have prime $\mathfrak m_C$ and residue map $\mathrm{id}_K$; uniqueness in that node makes them equal. Likewise $a_Rb_R=\mathrm{id}_{D_R}$. Hence $a_R$ is an isomorphism. Any $R$-algebra isomorphism $a$ with $q_Ra=q$ has $a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{D_R})=\ker q=\mathfrak m_C$ and the same residue map, so that uniqueness also proves the asserted uniqueness among isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit), applied in both directions and to the two composites; the proof of Tag 08HT (lemma-uniqueness-henselian)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-etale-triples-colimit-is-strict-henselization] to the colimit $D_R$ for each $R$. Its base is local, its prime is $\mathfrak m_R$, and the residue embedding and every cocone leg have the prescribed $R$-action. Thus $D_R$ has the pointed-algebra colimit presentation of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Compose its defining algebra isomorphism to the pointed colimit with $a_R$ to obtain that presentation for $C$. This is precisely the defining condition, and its residue map is $q$ since $q_Ra_R=q$.

source.place: Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different), pointed-algebra interpretation of the triple colimit; Tag 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h), conclusion

proof.text: By step 2, $D_A$ is henselian local and $A\to D_A$ is local. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] therefore gives a unique local $A$-map $j:H\to D_A$. The composite $a_Ah$ is another such map: it extends $A\to D_A$ by $A$-linearity of $a_A$, and it is local because both $h$ and $a_A$ are local. Consequently $a_Ah=j$, which proves compatibility with the canonical $H$-structure.
